notes: REV1.4 BRANDED NAMING PASS — ADOPTED AS PRODUCT OF RECORD BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-21. This artifact changes display_name on the 64 currently runtime-eligible definitions and adds a public_question to each of them. It changes NOTHING else: no key, no predicate, no metric_expression, no threshold, no scope, no evaluator shape, no eligibility flag, no rollover flag, no tie rule. Field-by-field comparison against pool_catalog_rev1_3.json across all 80 definitions and the retired block reports ZERO governed-field drift, and test_s4_pool_catalog_unit.py asserts that comparison on every run.

KEYS ARE UNTOUCHED, PER POR §1.8. "A key is an immutable identifier and does not track a display name." Every persisted pool_instance reference therefore survives adoption unchanged, and betting.pool_rotation.digest_for hashes definition_key — never display_name — so the weekly rotation ordering of any league is bit-identical before and after.

THE 16 NON-DRAWABLE DEFINITIONS ARE PRESERVED VERBATIM. Three are dependency_state BLOCKED (#7, #46, #85) and thirteen are ENABLED but source-mapping incomplete (#32, #33, #34, #37, #41, #49, #53, #59, #60, #61, #75, #79, #80). None can be drawn, so none was renamed and none carries a public_question. They keep their Rev 1.3 names so that a later revision, made when their data dependency resolves, is a clean diff.

PUBLIC_QUESTION IS A GOVERNED PEER PRESENTATION FIELD. It exists because the app previously derived its pick prompt from scope alone — "Which team do you think takes this Prop Pool?" — which does not tell a GM what the contest measures. THE CATALOG IS AUTHORITATIVE: no surface may compose a question from scope, key or display_name. It carries NO settlement authority whatsoever; where a question and a predicate, metric_expression or threshold_condition could be read as disagreeing, the governed field wins and the question is the defect. Configurable thresholds (#89, #90, #91, #94) say "the target" rather than a literal, because a league that reconfigured one would otherwise be shown a number its own settlement does not use.

CONFIGURABLE THRESHOLDS ARE NOT RESTATED IN THE QUESTION. #89, #90, #91 and #94 carry threshold_configurable: true, so their questions say "the target" rather than a literal. A league that reconfigures one would otherwise be shown a number its own settlement does not use. The exact condition still renders from threshold_condition on the Pool detail surface.

KICKER NAMES — SUPERSEDED BY OWNER RULING 2026-08-21. Rev 1.3 §1.8 fixed #18 "Highest Scoring Kicker" and #77 "Highest Scoring Kicker Matchup" BY NAME. The owner ruling of 2026-08-21 supersedes that NAMING ruling: #18 is now "Kicker Chaos" and #77 is now "Kicker Duel". The proposal’s "Double Kickers" for #77 was refused. THE SCORING BASIS IS UNCHANGED AND WAS NOT OPEN: both still settle on actual Yahoo fantasy points via the canonical operand kicking_points, never on field-goal counts, never on made-field-goal distance, never on a 3xFG + 1xXP reconstruction. The Rev 1.3 §1.8 SCORING ruling survives verbatim and the persisted keys most_kicking_points and highest_combined_kicker_points are unchanged. See POR Rev 1.4 §2.

GLOBAL STARTER-SLOT RULE: unless a definition expressly requires otherwise, count only players or defenses occupying active starter slots. Exclude bench, IR, taxi and all other non-starting rostered assets. Flex and Superflex count by the actual player occupying the starting slot. Count each starter once. Carried on every row as starter_slot_rule.
GRAMMAR: the closed SUM/RATIO grammar is preserved unchanged. Formulas outside it carry a distinct governed evaluator_shape and are not expressible as metric_expression strings.

TOUCHDOWN SEMANTICS: total_touchdown_credits counts fantasy touchdown credits, not unique NFL scoring plays. A QB-to-receiver touchdown between two active starters yields two credits. Owner ruling Q-VOCAB-1, intentional.

CATALOG COMPLETENESS PRINCIPLE (binding): every Pool definition must be complete and deterministic at the product level. Commissioner configuration may enable or disable a governed definition, but may not supply a missing formula, threshold, data meaning, scoring interpretation, winner rule or settlement behavior. A definition requiring commissioner interpretation to become mathematically complete is not eligible for the active catalog: it must be completed by owner ruling or retired under zero-based budgeting.

RETIRED under that principle: #8, #9, #10, #11, #12 carried unbound threshold_value predicates. Numbers preserved permanently, never reused, not replaced in this revision. #89, #90, #91 and #94 are NOT retired: they carry explicit governed thresholds (10, 500, 700, 100) and require no commissioner interpretation.

TWO GATES, distinct. GATE 1 definition_runtime_eligible is PERSISTENT definition metadata: product-ENABLED, required_stats resolved, every required stat authoritatively source-mapped, and product_complete (mathematically complete without commissioner interpretation). GATE 2 league_activation_ready is TRANSIENT environment state keyed by league, provider and definition or required-source set, carrying a measurement timestamp. IT IS NOT STORED ON A DEFINITION and does not appear in the definitions array. The selector requires BOTH. GATE-1 COUNT IS A CEILING, NOT A FORECAST: 64 is the current Gate-1 ceiling. Restoring provider access clears one Gate-2 precondition only and does not by itself return any definition to selectable status. The selectable count must be recomputed after every Gate-2 requirement is satisfied for the particular league, provider and definition or required-source set. It is never stated in advance. See current_environment for the dated snapshot; the Gate-2 persistence carrier is implementation scope.

KICKER SCORING BASIS (owner ruling 2026-08-01, binding). #18 Highest Scoring Kicker and #77 Highest Scoring Kicker Matchup both settle on actual Yahoo fantasy football points scored under the league's governing Yahoo scoring settings, via the canonical operand kicking_points. #18 compares the active starting kicker of each TEAM subject. #77 sums the actual Yahoo fantasy points of the two active starting kickers in each scheduled MATCHUP subject. Neither is computed from raw field-goal counts, field-goal distance, or any 3xFG + 1xXP reconstruction. The persisted keys most_kicking_points and highest_combined_kicker_points are unchanged; a key is an immutable identifier and does not track a display name.

TIE PAYOUT REMAINDER (owner ruling 2026-08-01, binding). tie_rule EVEN_SPLIT is fully specified and carries no implementation discretion. base_share_cents = floor(pot_cents / winner_count). remainder_count = pot_cents % winner_count. Every winner receives base_share_cents. The first remainder_count winners, ordered by canonical GM identifier ascending, each receive one additional cent. The ordering key is the stable canonical GM identifier, never a display name, roster position, claim order, or database-return order. The full pot is conserved and distributed exactly once. Ties settle and never roll. A retry must reproduce the identical allocation. Governed at POR §6.3.

SETTLEMENT IDEMPOTENCY (binding on any future implementation). Every economic settlement or sweep generated by a pool instance must post its ledger entries and transition pool_instance.settled inside one atomic database transaction, and must carry an event-keyed idempotency key protected by a database uniqueness constraint. A row lock may supplement that protocol but never replaces it. Governed at POR §6.4 and Scope §G1.

made_field_goal_distance is retained in the stat vocabulary as unsupported historical and source documentation only. It is not an operand of any active catalog definition and blocks no active Pool. Its former dependents #97 and #98 are retired.

WP1B POSTSEASON ELIGIBILITY, 2026-08-13. postseason_eligible was null on all 80 active definitions, which POR §C1 rules as NOT YET ELIGIBLE and which left the postseason candidate set empty. It is now resolved to an explicit boolean on every row. TRUE on the 44 definitions that are (a) dependency_state ENABLED, (b) definition_runtime_eligible, and (c) not MATCHUP/RANK_EXTREMUM. FALSE on the other 36. The MATCHUP/RANK_EXTREMUM exclusion is the WP1B §5 prohibition on matchup-vs-matchup Pools — those definitions make whole matchups the competing options, which the postseason POR forbids; MATCHUP/QUALIFIER is unaffected because each matchup qualifies independently. No other field on any row changed, and no definition was added, retired or renumbered. betting/pool_catalog.load_catalog now refuses to load any catalog that marks a MATCHUP/RANK_EXTREMUM row postseason_eligible, so this exclusion cannot be undone by a later edit.

OWNER NAMING AMENDMENTS, 2026-08-21, binding. Four proposal names were revised on adoption: #48 "Workload" → "Heavy Usage"; #77 "Double Kickers" → "Kicker Duel"; #78 "Efficiency Battle" → "Touch Efficiency"; #94 "Two Ground Games" → "Ground Tandem". #18 "Kicker Chaos" was approved as proposed. Every other proposal name — including the ones the proposal itself flagged for owner attention — is owner-accepted as written.

FEWEST-vs-ZERO NAMING CONVENTION, 2026-08-21, binding. MIN / FEWEST contests use ordinary branded football language. EXACT-ZERO qualifiers reserve "Free" terminology, and no MIN contest may use it. The active set is exactly six MIN contests (#28 Clean Pocket, #29 Sure Hands, #30 Ball Security, #62 No Picks, #83 Sticky Fingers, #86 Ball Control) and three exact-zero qualifiers (#84 Fumble Free, #87 Turnover Free, #95 Pick Free). #84 was renamed from the proposal’s "Clean Hands" to satisfy the convention; the other eight already did. THE NAME DESCRIBES THE EXISTING MECHANIC — no predicate, direction, threshold or evaluator shape was altered to fit a name.

WEEKLY SCOPE COMPOSITION, 2026-08-21, binding — see weekly_slate_composition below and POR Rev 1.4 §4.2. The normal four-Pool REGULAR-phase weekly slate is 3 TEAM + 1 MATCHUP, replacing the 1 TEAM + 3 MATCHUP the unconstrained digest ranking happened to produce. This is a governed ROTATION rule, not a presentation filter: it is applied inside betting.pool_rotation.build_week_slate before any row is written. Selection stays deterministic — the SHA-256 digest serialization, its tie-breakers and the carried-key subtraction are all untouched. The composition decides HOW MANY fresh slots each scope receives; the existing ranking decides WHICH definitions fill them. Catalog eligibility is not weakened, blocked and source-incomplete definitions remain non-drawable, no definition may appear twice in one slate, rollover behaviour is unchanged and economics are unchanged.

weekly_slate_composition._note: POR Rev 1.4 §4.2, binding. The scope composition of the normal four-Pool REGULAR-phase weekly slate. THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: it is the governed priority in which fresh-slot deficits are satisfied when rollover continuations have already over-filled a scope, so the outcome is deterministic in every carry configuration. Read by betting.pool_slate and handed to the pure selector; betting.pool_catalog refuses to load a catalog whose block disagrees with betting.pool_rotation.DEFAULT_SCOPE_MIX, so the artifact and the code cannot drift.
weekly_slate_composition.shortfall_rule: CROSS_SCOPE_FALLBACK. "Exactly 4 active Pools per fantasy week" (POR §4) is the stronger invariant. If a scope cannot fill its share from its own unused eligible candidates, the shortfall is filled from the remaining candidates of the other scope through the SAME digest ranking. A cycle reset is still signalled only when the TOTAL unused eligible set cannot fill the total fresh slots.
weekly_slate_composition.postseason_rule: NOT APPLIED. The postseason subset is fixed and the championship round is themed by CHAMPIONSHIP_PREFERRED_KEYS (WP1B §12); imposing a scope quota there would fight the theme. The composition governs the REGULAR phase four-slot slate only.
